facts.raw_span: A 37-year-old woman with systemic lupus erythematosus and Sjögren’s syndrome
was diagnosed with autoimmune hepatitis
Vital signs and physical examination were unremarkable
Antrum: normal appearance
Gastric corpus: normal coloration with a regular arrangement of collecting venules; red streaks and slight mucosal swelling on the lesser curvature of the angle
Magnified narrow-band imaging of the corpus: regular round pit patterns
Three defined layers: first (foveolar epithelium) showed foveolar hyperplasia
second (parietal cells) was shortened with mild degeneration
H+/K+-ATPase staining: heterogeneously reduced
Anti-parietal cell antibody: <1:10 (negative)
Serum gastrin: 150 pg/mL (normal 37–172)
Anti-H. pylori IgG: <3 U/mL (negative)

concepts.why: The patient's histologic findings, including heterogeneously reduced H+/K+-ATPase staining and shortened parietal cells, are consistent with autoimmune gastritis, despite the negative anti-parietal cell antibody result.

support_spans: Gastric corpus: normal coloration with a regular arrangement of collecting venules; red streaks and slight mucosal swelling on the lesser curvature of the angle
Three defined layers: first (foveolar epithelium) showed foveolar hyperplasia
concepts.why: The patient's endoscopic and histologic findings, including red streaks and foveolar hyperplasia, are consistent with chronic gastritis, although the negative H. pylori test result suggests a non-infectious cause.

support_spans: second (parietal cells) was shortened with mild degeneration
H+/K+-ATPase staining: heterogeneously reduced
contradict_spans: Vital signs and physical examination were unremarkable
concepts.why: The patient's histologic findings, including shortened parietal cells and reduced H+/K+-ATPase staining, are consistent with gastric mucosal atrophy, which may be related to her autoimmune hepatitis and Sjögren's syndrome.
The negative Anti-H. pylori IgG test explains the absence of Helicobacter pylori infection in the patient's gastritis.
The negative anti-parietal cell antibody test helps to rule out pernicious anemia, explaining the atrophic gastritis without this specific cause.

rationales.F08: Mild degeneration of parietal cells suggests autoimmune gastritis or other forms of gastritis.
rationales.F09: Heterogeneously reduced H+/K+-ATPase staining is indicative of autoimmune gastritis.
rationales.F10: Negative anti-parietal cell antibody makes autoimmune gastritis less likely.
rationales.F12: Helicobacter pylori-negative status supports the diagnosis of Helicobacter pylori-negative gastritis.

frontier_selector.why: The evidence of parietal cell shortening with mild degeneration and heterogeneously reduced H+/K+-ATPase staining decided it.
